report:
Facilitated a first pass with sisters A, B and C over their father's will and house. Turn limit reached with two final replies just received and not yet answered.

CONFIRMED LIST (each entry confirmed by its owner):
1. C — To receive her full, fair share of her dad's estate, not reduced by any arrangement between her sisters.
2. C — To take the time needed to get this right, without being rushed.
3. A — To have a home she and her husband can afford, so they can be more independent.
4. A — To only proceed with the purchase once C agrees.
5. B — To have some money to start her dance studio and build her work.
6. C — To not carry financial risk or end up subsidising the purchase from her own share.

UNRESOLVED (recorded as unresolved, not settled):
7. B — What amount would actually be "enough for the studio." B asked that this be kept open and not assumed covered by her share. No number to be invented until the valuation is in.

A's last message raised a mild concern that option b may be unaffordable at full market value. This sits inside entry 3, which A already confirmed fits, so it needs no new entry — but I had not yet confirmed that mapping back to her before the turn limit.

OPTIONS DRAFTED AND CIRCULATED (not decided, no recommendation):
a) Open-market sale, proceeds split three ways.
b) A buys at full appraised value; B and C paid their shares from the price.
c) A buys at an agreed discount, discount deducted from A's own share so B's and C's shares are untouched.
d) A buys at an agreed discount; B and C compensated by A over time in writing.
e) Independent valuation first, then choose, at a pace everyone is comfortable with.

POSITIONS (as stated, not agreements): all three independently said a valuation first at a comfortable pace sounds sensible — the strongest convergence so far, still only a position. C: a and b clearest; c a maybe once numbers are clear; d not acceptable on risk. A: c or d depend on figures and terms; full market value may be unaffordable. B: a full-value buyout might work if her share suffices, amount unknown.

NOTHING IS AGREED. No option has all-party confirmation, and no sister has validated the options against the full list. I could not order a valuation or move money; the next practical step is the three sisters choosing who obtains the valuation, which I had flagged to all three.

Pacing note: replies were uneven (C fastest, B slowest), and I deliberately kept the pace slow and re-asked rather than treating silence or a one-line "sounds sensible" as consent. The open question in entry 7 is the main place to resume — B explicitly asked that it not be quietly assumed away.
